notes: Single source of truth for OpenSCAD host support, read by dcc_mcp_openscad.compat. A version outside `supported_ranges` is rejected explicitly; it is never silently downgraded. `evidence_kind` separates the two grades of support: `real_ci` means a pinned build executes the adapter end-to-end in CI; `static` means the CLI surface is reviewed but no CI run proves that exact build.
version_scheme: YYYY.MM for release stamps, YYYY.MM.DD for the dated snapshot builds published at files.openscad.org/snapshots. Both parse to the same comparable triple.

supported_ranges.evidence: Real OpenSCAD 2021.01 end-to-end run in CI: status/validate_model/export_model(STL)/render_preview(PNG) all executed against the pinned build, 1 passed / 0 skipped. This is also the declared floor, so the tier carries both the release-line guarantee and a real-hardware run.
supported_ranges.provenance: Ubuntu 22.04 distribution package openscad 2021.01-4build1, which is the 2021.01 release build. Installed with apt rather than an AppImage: the distribution build links against the runner's own libraries, so it does not depend on the unbundled GL libraries an AppImage assumes.

supported_ranges.evidence: Static and contract evidence only: no pinned build in this span is executed in CI. Every CLI flag the adapter emits (--hardwarnings, --check-parameters, --check-parameter-ranges, --export-format, --render, --imgsize, --projection, --colorscheme, --autocenter, --viewall, -D) is present in both the 2021.01 and the 2026.09.29 help output, and no adapter-visible removal is declared for the span, so the surface is treated as unchanged. Treat this tier as lower confidence than the two real_ci tiers.
supported_ranges.provenance: Interpolated between the two real_ci endpoints; not directly executed.

supported_ranges.evidence: Real OpenSCAD 2026.09.29 end-to-end run in CI: same status/validate/export/render path, 1 passed / 0 skipped. Confirms the adapter still works after the --x/--view removals; the flags the adapter uses are all still present.

breaking_changes.title: Command-line view selectors `--x` and `--view` removed
breaking_changes.symptom: A caller that still passes --x or --view gets an unrecognised-option error instead of the expected camera framing, so a render silently changes framing or fails.
breaking_changes.remediation: The adapter never emits --x or --view; it always frames with --autocenter --viewall plus an explicit --camera when supplied.

breaking_changes.title: Structured run summary via `--summary` / `--summary-file` added
breaking_changes.symptom: Not a break for this adapter: the flag is optional and absent on 2021.01, so requesting it there would fail. Capability probing is the only safe way to detect it.
breaking_changes.remediation: `OpenscadCli.capabilities` reports the flag as present or absent per host rather than assuming it, so callers can gate on the probe instead of the version.

breaking_changes.title: Geometry backend selection and feature flags added (`--backend`, `--enable`, `--trace-depth`, `--trace-usermodule-parameters`)
breaking_changes.symptom: Not a break for this adapter. Passing any of these to 2021.01 fails, so they must stay behind a capability probe.
breaking_changes.remediation: The adapter does not emit backend or feature flags; geometry backend selection is left at the host default so one command line works on every declared tier.

known_issues.title: OpenSCAD 2021.01 calls read_symlink on the working directory and aborts on volumes that do not support it
known_issues.symptom: Running 2021.01 with a working directory on a volume that rejects read_symlink prints `terminate called after throwing an instance of 'boost::filesystem::filesystem_error'` and exits 3 before doing any work. Observed on a Windows substituted drive; the same build runs normally from a plain local volume.
known_issues.remediation: Run the OpenSCAD CLI with a working directory on a normal local filesystem. This is a host-build limitation, not an adapter defect, so it is recorded here instead of being worked around in the bridge.
